description: Ensure /var/tmp/gym-scratch is created automatically at boot, owned by root:root with mode 0750. Its contents must be eligible for cleanup after {number} days. Apply the rule now.
Ensure system journal entries survive reboots and journal storage is limited to 200 MiB. Apply the configuration to the running journal service.
checks: systemd-analyze cat-config systemd/journald.conf | awk -F= '/^[[:space:]]*Storage=/ {s=$2} /^[[:space:]]*SystemMaxUse=/ {m=$2} END {exit !(s=="persistent" && (m=="200M" || m=="209715200"))}'

description: The gym-reporter.service unit fails to start. Repair it so it starts successfully now and at every boot.
hint: Inspect systemctl status, journalctl and the unit definition.
setup:
printf '[Unit]
Description=Gym report service
[Service]
Type=oneshot
RemainAfterExit=yes
ExecStart=/usr/bin/gym-missing-command
[Install]
WantedBy=multi-user.target
' > /etc/systemd/system/gym-reporter.service; systemctl daemon-reload; systemctl disable --now gym-reporter.service 2>/dev/null || true; systemctl start gym-reporter.service || true

description: The gym-schedule.timer is broken. Make it execute gym-schedule.service every minute and start automatically at boot. Verify that its service has run.
setup:
printf '[Service]
Type=oneshot
ExecStart=/usr/bin/touch /var/log/gym-schedule.done
' > /etc/systemd/system/gym-schedule.service; printf '[Timer]
OnCalendar=invalid
[Install]
WantedBy=timers.target
' > /etc/systemd/system/gym-schedule.timer; rm -f /var/log/gym-schedule.done; systemctl daemon-reload; systemctl disable --now gym-schedule.timer 2>/dev/null || true

description: Configure the running SSH server to disallow root login and password authentication while allowing public-key authentication. The settings must persist.
setup:
mkdir -p /etc/ssh/sshd_config.d; printf 'PermitRootLogin yes
PasswordAuthentication yes
PubkeyAuthentication no
' > /etc/ssh/sshd_config.d/00-gym.conf; systemctl enable --now sshd; systemctl reload sshd

description: Configure the default boot target to multi-user.target without changing the currently active target.
Mount the NFS export localhost:/srv/gym-export at /mnt/gym-nfs. Make the mount persistent and ensure its report.txt is readable.
setup: mkdir -p /srv/gym-export /mnt/gym-nfs /etc/exports.d; echo gym-nfs-ok > /srv/gym-export/report.txt; echo '/srv/gym-export 127.0.0.1(ro,sync)' > /etc/exports.d/gym.exports; systemctl enable --now nfs-server; exportfs -ra; umount /mnt/gym-nfs 2>/dev/null || true; sed -i '\|[[:space:]]/mnt/gym-nfs[[:space:]]|d' /etc/fstab

description: Configure /srv/gym-auto/reports to mount localhost:/srv/gym-auto-export on demand. The automounter must start at boot.
setup: mkdir -p /srv/gym-auto-export /etc/exports.d /etc/auto.master.d; echo gym-auto-ok > /srv/gym-auto-export/report.txt; echo '/srv/gym-auto-export 127.0.0.1(ro,sync)' > /etc/exports.d/gym-auto.exports; systemctl enable --now nfs-server; exportfs -ra; rm -f /etc/auto.master.d/gym.autofs /etc/auto.gym; systemctl enable --now autofs; systemctl restart autofs

description: Export /srv/gym-share read-only via NFS to 192.0.2.25 only. Ensure the export is active and survives reboot.
setup: mkdir -p /srv/gym-share /etc/exports.d; echo '/srv/gym-share *(rw,sync)' > /etc/exports.d/gym-share.exports; systemctl enable --now nfs-server; exportfs -ra
